title: Grab and Move doesn't play nice with Photoshop
summary: Grab and Move reportedly interferes with Photoshop Alt gestures; a newer commenter also sees Alt held until another key or release in a keyboard checker, even with Photoshop excluded.

judgment.rationale: The thread establishes an Alt symptom but not that Grab and Move causes the cross-window keyboard-checker behavior. Because the reporter has already tested Photoshop exclusion and a different app surface, the next discriminating comparison is the same Alt test with Grab and Move disabled.
evidence: The reporter uses Alt for Photoshop Clone-tool source selection and reports delayed Alt behavior with Grab and Move enabled.
A commenter says switching the activation modifier to Win avoided the Photoshop interaction; custom modifiers were suggested.
The latest commenter reports the behavior also in keyboardchecker.com and says photoshop.exe was already excluded.
judgment.recommended_action: Request the enabled/disabled Alt comparison before choosing a hook change.

fix_assessment.rationale: A focused comparison can establish whether an applicable Grab and Move fix is warranted; current evidence does not justify a specific hook change.

proposed_fixes.title: Preserve ordinary Alt behavior with Grab and Move enabled
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: Grab and Move's Alt modifier-session handling may alter the Alt key-up/down path for some foreground applications; the cross-window observation leaves an external input interaction possible.
plan: Compare the same Alt test with Grab and Move enabled and disabled on a current build.
If behavior differs, trace modifier hook dispositions and exclusion handling for that exact foreground window.
Change only the confirmed event path and add a focused regression case for Alt passthrough.
verification: The same Alt key-down behavior is observed with Grab and Move enabled and disabled, while the intended Alt-drag workflow still works.

confidence.rationale: Current source contains a relevant Alt hook, but the latest cross-window test and existing app exclusion leave causality unresolved.

information_gaps.information: Whether Alt behaves normally with Grab and Move fully disabled when repeating the same keyboardchecker.com test.
information_gaps.why_needed: This comparison determines whether to investigate Grab and Move's low-level hook or an Alt behavior that persists independently.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Temporarily disable Grab and Move, repeat the held-Alt test in keyboardchecker.com, re-enable it, and report both results. No logs are needed for this comparison.

actions.label: Confirm Alt behavior with Grab and Move disabled

comment.body: Thanks for testing the Photoshop exclusion and checking Alt in keyboardchecker.com. That shows the symptom is not limited to Photoshop, but it does not yet show whether Grab and Move causes it. Could you repeat the same held-Alt test with Grab and Move fully disabled, then enabled again, and report whether key-down is recognized before another key is pressed? This distinguishes a Grab and Move hook interaction from an Alt behavior that persists independently; no additional logs are needed for this comparison.
